## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `81d3d66184cadb1cd0b1f09cafa188f4825df972`
Local-runs: none
Scope: scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs + scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs, scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs

Read for this record: card #36483 (body, triage 7080802379, claim 7136432186, dev report 7139220335; no ruling and no earlier record on the thread), the PR body and its three-file list, the net diff `a73edb3c..81d3d661` (+297/-1), and the 49 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Code outside the diff was read at the head, never reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-protection.zod.ts`, the three pinned tests and their packages' vitest configs, `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, and the engine's `readReadmeNetBase`, `readTrackedSource` and `changedPathsFromGit`.

Check-runs on the head: every run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. The ones that answer this diff: `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` success (the instrument's own battery, both tiers), `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` success, `Test Core` success (shards 1/10 and 2/10 and the aggregate), `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success, `Check Changeset` success, `PR-body guards` success, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` aggregates success.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Derived command set, widened: right.** A change set whose diff moves the top-level members of `FieldSchema`'s shape, or of the `MetadataProtectionFields` literal it spreads, now derives three more commands (the driver-sql, metadata-core and metadata-protocol pins). This is the card's first arm. All three files exist at the head, each sits in the package its `--filter` names, and each really pins the whole set: `builtin-column-collision.test.ts` compares `Object.keys(FieldSchema.shape)` with `FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS` both ways; `object-schema-fls-references.test.ts` does the same against `FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` (lines 792 to 830); the metadata-protocol control pins `field: 87`.
- **Run-record accept set, narrowed: right.** `--ran` now refuses a record that lacks one of the three when the row fires. A record that was accepted before on such a diff is exactly the green-locally, red-in-CI record the card was filed against.
- **Quiet set: right.** An edit that leaves the members alone (prose, a `.describe()`, a refine, a nested schema, the options argument, a reorder) derives nothing; an unchanged file derives nothing, which includes a surface named at dispatch before code exists. The second is a deliberate asymmetry and it is the posture two rows already on `main` take (`stampsAnErrorCodeLiteral`, the README claim net).
- **Wide set: right.** A created or deleted declaring file, or a declaration the reader cannot place on either side, derives the row.
- **Public surface: none.** The four new exports (`objectLiteralMembers`, `declaredKeySet`, `changesFieldSchemaKeySet`, `FIELD_SCHEMA_KEY_DECLARATIONS`) are exports of a script under `scripts/pm`, consumed by its own self-test. No package source, no schema, no generated output moves.

### ② Semver level

No changeset, `skip-changeset` label: correct. The diff is three files under `scripts/pm`, the root package is private and no published package ships that directory, so nothing is published. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: no — agreed. The diff changes no published contract; it changes which commands an internal instrument derives.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report; nothing to answer.
- Deviation, diff-read predicate in place of a path match: accepted. The binding text the claim cites warns that a hand-kept map of what a test really reads is a second thing that goes stale. `FIELD_SCHEMA_KEY_DECLARATIONS` is such a map, but its staleness is loud on both sides: a declaration that moves makes `declaredKeySet` answer null, which derives the row on any change to the file, and the self-test's live cases (every row reads on this tree; the census against the driver table) red in the instrument's own lane.
- Deviation, quiet at dispatch time: accepted, see ①.
- Deviation, census pin moved from 753 to 755: correct. The diff adds exactly two lines above that position in `dispatch-gates.mjs`, the data import and its re-export.
- Deviation, PR-body footer form: prose on the PR body, outside this record's scope.
- Out-of-scope finding, the wider family (the same metadata-protocol control counts object, flow, page, agent and other types, and a key added to one of those derives nothing): the dev report carries it with no carrier, noted in the PR body only. Escalated to the seat: it is the same failure class as this card and should have a follow-up card as its carrier, since a PR body is not a queue. It is not a finding against this diff, whose card is `field` only.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff reads two source files and one git blob per declaring path; it touches no data path, materialises no ids and joins nothing.

### ④ Design judgment

**`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (hits).** Read against the code it cites and against the card's scenario (a dev re-deriving off the merge base after adding a `FieldSchema` key).

- `declaredKeySet` against the live declaration: `FieldSchema` is `lazySchema` over a body whose first `strictObject(` call takes the options literal and then the shape, so `call: 'strictObject', argument: 1` lands on the shape; the options argument is stepped over at the call's own depth on the masked text, where the long guidance strings cannot contribute a comma or a brace. `MetadataProtectionFields` is a bare literal after its `=`. The binding regex stops at the first `=`, which is the assignment, not the arrow. Holds.
- `objectLiteralMembers`: reads over `maskCommentsAndLiterals`, which blanks comment and literal content and keeps delimiters and offsets, so the quoted-key branch can pair quotes and read the name back from the source. Tried against it: a trailing comma before the closing brace (no member, clean return); keys named `get`, `set` or `async` (the prefix group needs whitespace and a following name, so the key itself is read); shorthand before the closing brace; a comma inside type arguments at depth zero (opens a phantom member only when followed by a generic or a quoted type, identically on base and head, so it can add noise on an edit to those type arguments and can never hide a key); an unbalanced close (null, which reads wide). No path found by which a key added, removed or renamed at the top level of either literal compares equal.
- `changesFieldSchemaKeySet`: both sides absent is false (the hypothetical surface), one side absent is true, an unreadable declaration on either side is true, otherwise sorted member lists compared. A rename of the file reaches it through both names, since the no-path derivation lists moves with `--no-renames`. Agrees with its docblock sentence by sentence, with the two notes below.
- Registration: `'field-schema-key-set'` in `CHANGE_KIND_PREDICATES` matches the row's `matches`; the import and the re-export are the only other edits.

**`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs` (implementing).** The row follows the `spec-migration-entry` precedent field for field (`ciJob: 'Test Core'`, `ciRunner: 'set -- pnpm turbo run test'`, `ciSubset`), and the runner string is the one `ci.yml` spells. The three `why` texts were checked against the tree: the driver-sql vitest config aliases every spec namespace to source and the test reaches the workspace only through spec and its own module, so no build is owed; the metadata-core config carries no alias, so it reads the built spec; the metadata-protocol config aliases only the sdui-parser, and its manifest lists spec plus six other workspace packages besides it, as the text says. The count pin's text says added or removed, not renamed, which is what a count can see. The deletion criterion and its two refusals (no widening to every reader of `FieldSchema.shape`, no fallback to a path match) are consistent with the row. The 48 and 9 replay figures in the docblock were not re-measured: this checkout's history is shallow and the review is read-only; nothing in the tree contradicts them.

**`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` (implementing, the battery that enforces the row).** The cases cover the member reader, the declaration reader, each edit shape in both directions with controls, the rendering, the runnable union, the `--ran` refusal per pin, the STALE branch, the load-time refusal of a mismatched `ciSubset`, and the live tree. The census pin move is correct. Green in `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` on this head.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract in the accepted scenario; each is left as an accepted deviation, since a fix would move the head:

- N1 (nit) — the `objectLiteralMembers` docblock says the live census holds the read against both closure tables. The self-test compares the reader's set with the driver-sql table only; `FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` is not read there. The equality still follows through the metadata-core test's own two-way pin, so the sentence overstates the battery, not the guarantee.
- N2 (nit) — the predicate's base is `readReadmeNetBase`, which falls back to `HEAD` when no merge base can be computed (documented on that reader, outside this diff). In such a checkout an explicit-path invocation reads a committed key change as unchanged, which is quiet where the new docblock's stated bias is wide. The dev's no-path re-derivation refuses outright in the same checkout and names the fetch, so the card's scenario is not reachable through it. The README claim net carries the same limit today.
- N3 (nit) — two shapes the member reader cannot see are not among the stated limits: a key contributed by a conditional spread of an inline literal, and a key added after the call by `.extend`. Neither exists in the two declarations at the head, and the live census reds in the instrument's lane the day one appears with its driver row.
- N4 (nit) — the live census makes the instrument's self-test red whenever the schema and the driver table disagree, a state the driver's own test already reds in Test Core. It is a second, earlier report of the same defect, not a new false red, but the case name is the only pointer a dev gets from that lane.
